$comment: Six units. js/ (fact-kit) and facts/ (fact-kit-facts) publish to npm; py/ (PyPI), rs/ (crates.io) and go/ (Go module) are the readers in other languages; the Swift reader is registered at the repository root (path ".") because SwiftPM only reads Package.swift there. Units are the keys of packages. A new unit needs an entry here, an entry in .release-please-manifest.json (0.0.0 until it first releases, so initial-version applies), an entry in release-policy.json and, when it publishes, a case in scripts/lib/release-stages.sh (unit_registry) and scripts/release/publish-units.sh; README.md lists the steps. The Swift unit has no component in its tag and no v (a bare X.Y.Z), because SwiftPM resolves versions from bare semver tags only and a v-prefixed root tag would be taken as a version. Its exclude-paths name every top-level directory that is not Swift, so a commit that touches only those does not release it (release-please matches directories only, not files); a new top-level directory must be added to that list, and release-config.test.ts fails until it is. A release/vX.Y branch carries the whole repository, cut-release.sh --units picks the units that board it, and scoped to the train this config holds only those. separate-pull-requests is false so the train gets a single Release PR with one changelog per unit; each unit keeps its own version and tag. Nothing is released from main.
